noAccess.title: No access to workspaces
noAccess.text: Workspaces, GPU time and JupyterHub come with projects. For most people a personal project from a budget that is approved at once is enough.

servers.title: Active workspaces
servers.intro: Your active workspaces in JupyterHub. Each active workspace ends by itself when it is not used, and at the latest after its environment's run time (see state).
servers.name: Workspace
servers.stopMessage: “{{name}}” is stopped. Files in the home stay, unsaved changes in open notebooks are lost.
servers.ends: Ends after {{idle}} without activity, in {{left}} at the latest.

usage.title: Usage
usage.hint: What workspaces reserved from {{from}} to {{to}}: server hours, vCPU, RAM and GPU hours, home size. Collected every minute; today is not complete yet.
usage.csvHint: The grouping shown as CSV, with the measured values.
usage.explain: What is charged is the reservation (requested cores and memory), as with flavors in OpenStack. “CPU used” relates the measured use to it. Home GB-days: space used, measured hourly, the day's largest value counts; a project's storage is listed as “Projektspeicher”.

image.buildOnSave: The build starts on saving (usually 5–15 minutes).
image.label: Environment
image.hint: What is installed on the project’s servers, the same for every server type. The server type only chooses the hardware (CPU, CPU with GPU kernel, GPU).
image.finishedHint: A publicly pullable image. Built on one of our bases (FROM registry.gpu.services.dhbw.cloud/platform/base-…) it runs with everything; any other runs as it is (it needs jupyterhub-singleuser), without “CPU + GPU kernel”.
image.notDerived: This image is not built on one of our bases: it runs as it is, without “CPU + GPU kernel” and without the DHBW extensions.
image.updateAvailable: The tag now points at a newer version. Running and new servers stay on the current one until it is taken.
image.autoUpdate: Take new versions of the tag automatically
image.autoUpdateHint: Otherwise a newer version is only shown and taken at the press of a button. New servers then start with it, running ones keep theirs.
image.gitHint: Built like Binder from requirements.txt, environment.yml, apt.txt and postBuild (top level, binder/ or .binder/) on the chosen base. The repository’s files reach the servers as “Material from Git” (below). A new version of the base triggers a rebuild; until a build is ready, the previous image stays.

material.title: Material from Git
material.hint: Fetched into ~/projects/<repository> and updated at every server start, without overwriting one’s own changes; JupyterLab opens that folder. Independent of the environment, so with an existing image too.

projects.limits: Limits per person (at the same time)
projects.limitsHint: Counted is what one person runs in this project at the same time. 0 means no limit – except for GPUs, where 0 means no GPU.
projects.budgetsHint: Tighter limits within the project quotas, e.g. at most 40 vCPU hours per person in 7 days, so nobody uses up the quota alone. Windows in calendar days: “today”, 7 or 30 days including today, “total” since the project was created. Once a limit is reached, no server starts and running servers end within 5 minutes (the home stays).
projects.profilesHint: What members can choose when starting a server in JupyterHub. The platform sets the list; GPU types count against the project's GPU quotas.
projects.adminOnlyHint: Server types, limits and usage limits are set by admins. The environment (base, project image, Git) and the material can be changed here.

storage.title: Storage (admins)
storage.hint: Workspace storage on JuiceFS: one volume per project with storage, plus homes from before the projects. Measured hourly.
storage.ofNode: of the node's {{total}} GB RAM · peak {{peak}} GB
storage.noReport: No measurement since the AI service last restarted; the next comes on the hour.
storage.explain: A project's limit is its workspace storage from the budget tree; a full volume refuses further writes. The metadata grow with the number of files (roughly 1 GB RAM per 2–3 million files); when RAM runs short, JuiceFS stops.

gpuHours.title: GPU use per hour
gpuHours.hint: How full the GPUs were, per hour in local time: colour = share held by workspaces; red outline = someone waited. Sampled every minute, kept 365 days.
gpuHours.hintProject: Who in the project held or waited for a GPU, and when, in the chosen period.
gpuHours.cell: {{day}}, {{hour}}:00–{{hour}}:59: workspaces {{share}}, gap filler {{inference}}, waiting on average {{avg}}, at most {{max}}
gpuHours.empty: No GPU use in this period.
gpuHours.explain: Counted is how long a GPU was assigned, not how much it computed. The gap filler (vLLM) uses a GPU as long as no workspace needs it and gives way at once. Waiting time: time in Kueue's queue until a GPU was free.

fleet.title: GPUs
fleet.intro: Every GPU node belongs to a pool (who the GPUs are for) and a tier (how large they are). Pool and tier make a GPU class: the budget tree grants it, and a server's start chooses it. More GPUs of an existing class need nothing in the tree; a node without pool takes no workspaces.
fleet.classesHint: Each class has its own queue and two resources in the budget tree. A class without nodes stays; its starts wait.
fleet.nodesHint: New GPU nodes appear here as soon as they are in the cluster. Changes apply to new pods within a minute; running ones stay where they are. The gap filler is an LLM that uses the GPU while no workspace needs it.
fleet.noNodes: No GPU nodes in the cluster.
fleet.poolsHint: “general” is for everybody; a pool of its own is for GPUs only certain budgets should get (grant them in the tree only there). The id becomes part of the tree resources; when it changes, the amounts in the tree move along. A pool that lends gives idle GPUs to the other pools of the same tier and takes them back as soon as it needs them.
fleet.poolIdInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter, 2–20 characters
fleet.renamePoolHint: The pool's GPU classes get new ids; budgets, projects and booked GPU hours move along, the gap filler restarts once.
fleet.poolKeptClassesTip: A GPU class comes into being as soon as a node is assigned to the pool. It is a resource of the budget tree and projects may hold budget for it; that is why classes and their pool stay, even without nodes.

start.title: Start workspace
start.intro: Choose project and environment. The choice is in this page's address: a link with project and environment can go to all members of the project.
start.booked: Computing time is booked to this project.
start.storage: The home directory belongs to the project ({{gb}} GB for all members together) and is the same in every environment; its folder project-shared is for all members. Deleting the project deletes these files too.
start.noStorage: This project has no workspace storage: files are lost when the workspace ends. Storage is requested at the project.
start.deletes: On {{date}} its workspaces are deleted with all files; save what matters before or have the project extended.

envs.cpu: Workspace on the CPU with JupyterLab and VS Code. Up to 4 CPU cores and 8 GB RAM.
envs.cpu-gpukernel: Notebook on the CPU; the kernel “Python 3 (GPU)” starts on a GPU when needed. GPU kernels end after 5 min without execution, losing their variables.
envs.gpu: Whole workspace on a GPU with JupyterLab and VS Code. Waits until a GPU is free.

start.noEnv: This project allows no environment. The project's managers set its environments.
start.linkHint: The link opens this page with the current choice; nothing starts before “Start”.
start.unknownProject: The project “{{project}}” from the link is not one of your active projects with workspaces. The project's managers add members.
start.unknownEnv: The environment “{{env}}” from the link is not allowed in this project.
start.waiting: The workspace is starting, usually in less than a minute. It opens here once it is ready.
start.waitingGpu: The workspace waits for a free GPU, then starts. It opens here once it is ready.
start.gone: The workspace could not start. The list of active workspaces shows what is running; starting again reports the reason.
start.limits: Ends after {{idle}} without activity, after {{max}} at the latest.
start.building: The environment's image is being built from the Git repository. Workspaces can start once the build is done; this page updates by itself.
start.buildFailedTitle: The environment could not be built
start.buildFailed: Without a built image no workspace can start in this project. Those who manage the project can fix the repository in the project settings (Workspaces) and build again.
start.linkHintAuto: The link starts the workspace with this choice as soon as it is opened; when one is already running there, it opens that one.
